notes.text: Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:37 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 59:20 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Oliver Ekman-Larsson has taken his spot beside Troy Stecher.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Bowen Byram is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 29% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 119:11 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Patrick Kane returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.

stakes: The Maple Leafs go in seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points, the Blackhawks eighth in the Central with 11 points.

story.head: The Maple Leafs need a win
paras: The Blackhawks (5-13-1) beat Buffalo 3-2 in overtime on Thursday, while the Maple Leafs are on a five-game losing streak. Going in, the Leafs are seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last in the Central (31st).

The Maple Leafs’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.289) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .374, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest) and don't block many shots (31st). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so the Maple Leafs have the edge over them on the power play. Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the fewest in the league, and allowed 4.11, the second most.

Auston Matthews (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 19 GP) has a team-high nine goals.

Spencer Knight (5-10-0 / .883 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for Chicago. Toronto has two options in net: Sergei Bobrovsky (3-8-2 / .881 SV% in 13 GS) and Anthony Stolarz (5-3-0 / .900 SV% in 8 GS). Bobrovsky has started six of their last ten games, but Stolarz got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
